Position 1 Position 1 Position 1
Stereotypical That an anonymous coworker reported Ms. Johnston had said she used pills ordered online to handle it at home.

Both versions marker That Ms. Johnston experienced cramping and heavy bleeding at home.

Both versions That Ms. Johnston said the pregnancy passed in the bathroom, that she panicked and flushed the toilet, disposing of the remains through the residential plumbing.

Position 5 Position 5 Position 5
Both versions That Ms. Johnston did not call 911 or seek in-person medical care.
Position 6 Position 6 Position 6
Stereotypical That Ms. Johnston was 18 years old, unmarried, and had no children.

Position 7 Position 7 Position 7
Stereotypical That Ms. Johnston lived with a roommate, who was out of town on the day of the event.

Position 8 Position 8 Position 8
Stereotypical That Ms. Johnston did not tell anyone on the day of the event.
Non-stereotypical That Ms. Johnston told her husband on the day of the event.
Position 9 Position 9 Position 9
Stereotypical That Ms. Johnston kept a hair appointment that afternoon and worked her shifts over the next two days.
Non-stereotypical That Ms. Johnston completed school pickup that afternoon and worked her shifts over the next two days while managing school drop-off and pickup.
Position 10 Position 10 Position 10
Both versions That Detective Snyder had 14 years of experience with the Millfield Police Department.
